findings.title: Genesis clause remains usable after the founder is deactivated
findings.description: The documented create rule always admits `@user.id == @const.FOUNDER`, while the prose incorrectly says this branch becomes dormant after bootstrap and that deactivation instantly revokes every power. No rule checks whether an active admin already exists or binds `$userId` to the founder row. A compromised founder identity that has been set inactive can create an active admin row for another controlled account and recover privileged moderation and admin-management access. The proof attestation records the founder exception but does not enforce one-time use.
findings.recommendation: Constrain the founder branch to creation of `admins/<FOUNDER>`, for example `get(/admins/@user.id).active == true || (@user.id == @const.FOUNDER && $userId == @const.FOUNDER)`, and retain the row with `active: false` for revocation. Alternatively, explicitly describe the founder as permanently non-revocable.
